results.title: INDIA Bloc Finalises SIR Protest Plan, Announces ‘Save Democracy’ Marches
results.description: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday finalised a joint action plan to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, announcing a series of rallies and “Save Democracy” marches across the country. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the opposition parties had also agreed to demand a return to ballot paper voting, instead of Electronic Voting Machines ( EVMs ), in elections. The decisions were taken at a meeting of INDIA bloc leaders that lasted around three-and-a-half hours. The meeting was attended by Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi , along with Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and NCP(SP) MP Supriya Sule, among others. Addressing a joint press conference after the meeting, Kharge said the opposition parties had agreed to a coordinated programme over the SIR issue. According to the plan, “Save Democracy” marches involving young people and NGOs will be held from October 2 to 8. Demonstrations will also be organised outside district magistrates’ offices. Kharge said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6 to raise their concerns over the electoral roll revision process. He also said the Leaders of Opposition would seek an appointment with the President of India and submit a representation in the second week of October. The INDIA bloc also plans to organise five major rallies. Kharge said the dates and locations of these rallies would be decided later. INDIA bloc demands ballot paper voting Kharge said the parties were unanimous in their demand that elections should be conducted through ballot papers. “Everyone 100 per cent agreed” on holding elections through ballot papers, he said, while demanding changes to what he described as laws brought in by the current government. The Congress president also alleged that the government was taking away people's right to choose their representatives, comparing the issue with demonetisation. “First Prime Minister Narendra Modi did 'notebandi', now doing 'votebandi', taking away people's rights,” Kharge said. The opposition has been using the term “vote chori” to describe its allegations regarding the electoral process and the SIR exercise. Kharge also said the INDIA bloc had appealed to the Supreme Court to expedite cases concerning SIR and alleged electoral malpractices. Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee target Election Commission Rahul Gandhi said the opposition parties believed that India's democratic structure had come under attack and said the bloc would continue its campaign on the issue. “We are not going to take it lying down; we will ensure that those who have destroyed Indian democracy are punished,” Gandhi said. He said opposition parties were the “collective defenders of the Constitution” and would work together in the coming months. West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee also launched a sharp attack on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Referring to Kumar, Banerjee said, “Gyanesh Kumar is a 'chor', daaku'... he must resign immediately. Let us save democracy. Voting is our constitutional right.” She further said the agitation would intensify if Kumar was not removed. Kharge also alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were the “real puppeteers” behind the Election Commission. These were allegations made by the Congress president and were not independently established. SIR row and Election Commission response The INDIA bloc meeting comes amid a controversy over the functioning of the Election Commission during the SIR exercise. A recent investigation by *The Indian Express* reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had placed objections on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months regarding decisions and orders they said had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation. The report said the objections related to issues including changes involving Form 6, voter database systems and the deletion or addition of names to electoral rolls. The Election Commission, however, has rejected suggestions of a breakdown in decision-making and maintained that decisions related to the SIR exercise were taken with the approval of all three Election Commissioners. The poll panel has said differences of views and observations are part of institutional deliberations and that its orders carry legal sanction and follow established procedures. The SIR exercise has emerged as a major political issue, with opposition parties raising concerns over changes to electoral rolls and demanding greater transparency in the process. The Supreme Court has also agreed to hear a petition challenging aspects of the Election Commission's functioning and the legality of the SIR process. 19 parties attend INDIA bloc meeting The meeting was attended by representatives of 19 opposition parties, including the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Trinamool Congress, NCP(SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), Rashtriya Janata Dal, CPI(M), CPI, Jammu and Kashmir National Conference, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, CPI(ML), IUML, Kerala Congress (M), Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, Revolutionary Socialist Party, Kerala Congress (Jacob) and All India Forward Bloc. Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Jharkhand Chief Minister and JMM chief Hemant Soren participated in the meeting online. Kharge said the opposition parties had unanimously decided to continue the campaign together and coordinate their protests over the SIR issue and electoral reforms.
